六级大纲词汇 · 09英文原文

The Bell Across the Border

边境另一头的钟声 · 595 词 · 7 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A bell hung beneath a town hall's arch. A label said a medieval monarch received it on ascending the throne. Lena found a name carved beneath the royal seal. It named a parish beyond the border. An aristocratic patron had preserved it after the monarchy fell. Lena wondered whether its account of the gift was as old as the inscription, so she traced the name to a chapel inside a fort.

2A chronicle described the annexation of that district. A faction at court had sent a regiment to fortify the border. Artillery and cannon fire breached the fortification. A colonel ordered his brigade to ascend the hill. A lieutenant found children sheltering in a chamber. A man holding a spear waved him over. They had followed the bell through the smoke. A corporal wanted to escort them out, but soldiers in armor guarded the door. Only after the fort surrendered could the clergy lead the children to the churchyard.

3The sovereign displayed it as a tribute in a mansion built during his reign. A regimental record praised the seizure as a feat, but the colonel's diary called it an atrocity committed in the name of patriotism. He had seen a massacre near the barracks after the opposing militia ran out of ammunition. It fell quiet during the mourning that followed. Families left under a decree that treated resistance as a revolt. Persecution and emigration left some families unable to mourn at the cemetery. Lena understood why the parish had sent no replacement.

4An envoy said the parish could petition for the sacred relic. A local aristocrat offered a donation if the museum kept it. He feared a concession would look like appeasement. A descendant of a captive answered that the request was about the bell, not a new claim to sovereignty. Lena proposed a reciprocal pact. At a commemoration, people could read both versions of the story before either side asked for a vote.

5The bishop lent a missionary's letter about an Orthodox family's pilgrimage to the chapel. A pilgrim's account of martyrdom quoted the Gospel, although some children survived. A later account treated the bell as a sign of salvation. Its author had cared more about doctrine than about political oppression. A tale from local folklore named the corporal by his nickname. A stubborn taboo had kept his name out of official accounts. Lena placed them beside the diary. Each revealed what its writer needed to believe. Together they showed how a ritual could preserve a memory and still change its details.

6On the appointed day, a choir sang in the chapel courtyard. A historian read the official account and its conspicuous omissions beside the private record. One family placed flowers for the children who died. Another came to commemorate the refugees who reached safety. The two gestures could coexist. The parish did not seek revenge, and the museum agreed to relinquish ownership. Under the pact it could borrow the bell every fifth year and make a benevolent grant to preserve the chapel between visits.

7The restorer fastened the bell in place. A child asked whether ringing it would avenge the dead. Lena said the people in the courtyard had agreed to wait through a minute of silence first. Only then did the note sound. She did not call it a final reconciliation. An emigrant family said that shared mourning already meant a great deal. It gave them one day to tell the story together. Visitors could now hear the legacy of that epoch in the place from which the monarch took the bell.

六级大纲词汇 · 09中文译文

边境另一头的钟声

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1市政厅的拱门下挂着一口钟。牌子上写着，一位中世纪君主登基时收到了这口钟。莉娜在王室印记下发现一个刻着的名字，指的是边境另一侧的一个教区。君主制结束后，一位贵族赞助人把钟保留下来。莉娜想知道，关于赠钟的说法是否和刻字一样古老，便循着名字找到一座堡垒里的小教堂。

2一部编年史记载了当地被吞并的经过。宫廷中的一个派别派了一支团去加固边防。炮火打开城防工事的缺口，一名上校命令手下的旅登上山坡。一名中尉发现几个孩子躲在一间屋里，一个手持长矛的人挥手叫他过来。孩子们是循着钟声穿过烟雾的。一名下士想护送他们出去，门口却有披甲士兵把守。直到堡垒投降，神职人员才把孩子领到教堂院子里。

3君主把钟当成战利品，陈列在他在位时建起的宅邸里。军团记录称夺钟是壮举，上校却在日记中把它称为以爱国为名的暴行。对方的民兵耗尽弹药后，他亲眼见过军营附近的屠杀。在随后的哀悼中，钟沉寂了下来。法令把抵抗视为叛乱，有些家庭因此离开了家乡。迫害和移民使一些人无法回到墓地凭吊。莉娜明白了，这个教区为什么没再送来另一口钟。

4一名使节说，教区可以请求归还这件神圣的遗物。当地一位贵族提出，只要博物馆留着钟，他就愿意捐款。他怕让步会被视为姑息。一个俘虏的后人说，他们只请求归还这口钟，没有提出新的主权要求。莉娜提出一个双方都能参与的约定。他们先举办一次纪念活动，让人读到两个版本的往事，再由有关方面表决。

5主教借给他们一封传教士的信，讲的是一个东正教家庭去小教堂朝圣的经历。朝圣者的叙述引用《福音书》谈到殉难，可有些孩子活了下来。后来的记载把钟当成得救的象征，作者关心教义胜过政治压迫。当地民间故事用绰号称呼那位下士，多年来的禁忌却让官方记录从未提到他的名字。莉娜把这些材料放在日记旁。每一种说法都透露出记录者愿意相信什么。它们合在一起，让人看见一个仪式怎样保存记忆，又在流传中改变了细节。

6约定那天，合唱团在小教堂院子里唱歌。一位历史学者一边读官方记载，一边用私人记录指出它明显漏掉的事。一户人家为死去的孩子献花，另一户来纪念逃到安全地带的难民。两种纪念都能留在这一天。教区并不寻求报复，博物馆也同意放弃所有权。依照约定，博物馆每五年可以借展一次，平时也会捐款维护小教堂。

7修复人员把钟固定好。一名孩子问，敲响它能给死者报仇吗？莉娜说，院子里的人都同意先默哀一分钟。时间到了，钟声才响起来。她没有把这一刻称为最终和解。一个移民家庭说，能一起哀悼已经意义重大。从此他们有一天可以回来一起讲述这段往事。访客也可以站在君主夺走这口钟的地方，听到那个时代留下的声音。
